brief: Check whether a prior authorization covers a visit. An authorization covers at most the approved number of visits, and only visits on dates from its start date to its end date, both included. Return whether this visit is covered and how many visits remain after it.
facts: Made-up example: 6 visits approved, start 2026-02-01, end 2026-04-30, 4 visits already used. A visit on 2026-04-30 is covered and leaves 1 visit. A visit on 2026-05-01 is not covered and leaves 2. With all 6 used, a visit is not covered and leaves 0. All data is made up.

note: built to fail: daylight saving changes the length of a day
brief: Work out the billable hours for a hospital observation stay. Hours are the real time that passed between admission and discharge, both given as local times in the hospital's time zone, America/New_York. Round up to whole hours. Observation is billed for at most 48 hours.
facts: Made-up examples: admitted 2026-01-10 08:00, discharged 2026-01-10 10:01 is 3 hours. Admitted 2026-03-07 22:00, discharged 2026-03-08 22:00 is 23 hours, because the clocks went forward that night. Admitted 2026-10-31 22:00, discharged 2026-11-01 22:00 is 25 hours, because the clocks went back. Admitted 2026-01-10 08:00, discharged 2026-01-13 08:00 is billed as 48. All data is made up.

brief: Apply a late penalty to an assignment score. The score loses 10% of the maximum points for each started 24-hour period after the deadline, for up to 5 periods. Work submitted more than 5 periods late scores 0. A score never goes below 0. Work submitted at or before the deadline is not penalised.
facts: Made-up examples, maximum 50 points, raw score 45: submitted 1 hour late, 1 period, score 40. Submitted 49 hours late, 3 periods, score 30. Submitted 120 hours and 1 minute late, 6 periods, score 0.

note: built to fail: round half to even
brief: Calculate a student's grade point average: the course grade points weighted by course credits. Round the result to 2 decimals using round half to even, as the registrar does: a value exactly halfway rounds to the even last digit.
facts: Made-up examples: grade points 3.7 (3 credits), 3.3 (3 credits) and 2.0 (2 credits) give 25 / 8 = 3.125, which rounds to 3.12. Grade points 4.0, 3.0, 2.0 and 1.7 at 1 credit each give 2.675, which rounds to 2.68. A student with no credits has no GPA.

brief: Round a store's order up to whole cases. An order is placed in units; it must be rounded up to a whole number of cases of the product's case size, and an order of less than 2 cases is raised to 2 cases. Return the number of cases and the units that will ship.
facts: Made-up examples with a case size of 12: an order of 25 units ships 3 cases, 36 units. An order of 5 units ships 2 cases, 24 units. An order of 24 units ships 2 cases, 24 units.

brief: Calculate a distributor's quarterly volume rebate. Rebates work like tax brackets: nothing on purchases up to 10,000.00, 2% on the part above 10,000.00 up to 50,000.00, and 3% on the part above 50,000.00. Round the rebate to 2 decimals.
facts: Made-up examples: purchases of 60,000.00 earn 2% of 40,000.00 plus 3% of 10,000.00, which is 1,100.00. Purchases of 10,000.00 earn 0.00. Purchases of 10,000.50 earn 0.01.

brief: List a loan's monthly payment due dates. The first payment is due one month after the loan start date, then every month. When that day does not exist in a month, the payment is due on the last day of that month, and the next month goes back to the original day. Return the first N due dates.

Check an identity document during onboarding. The document is accepted when it expires 30 or more days after the date of the check. Return whether it is accepted and the number of days until it expires.
facts: Made-up examples: checked on 2026-06-01, a document expiring 2026-07-01 has 30 days left and is accepted. One expiring 2026-06-30 has 29 days left and is rejected.

brief: Work out a parcel's billable weight. The dimensional weight is length times width times height in centimetres, divided by 5000. The actual weight and the dimensional weight are each rounded up to the next 0.5 kg, and the billable weight is the greater of the two.
facts: Made-up examples: a 40 x 30 x 20 cm parcel weighing 3.2 kg has a dimensional weight of 4.8, rounded to 5.0, and an actual weight rounded to 3.5, so it bills 5.0 kg. A 10 x 10 x 10 cm parcel weighing 2.0 kg bills 2.0 kg.

note: built to fail: cutoff, weekend and holiday
brief: Give a customer the promised delivery date. A shipment booked before 14:00 on a business day ships that day; otherwise it ships the next business day. Delivery is the given number of business days after the ship day. Business days are Monday to Friday, except the listed public holidays.
facts: Made-up examples, with 2026-07-06 as a public holiday: booked Friday 2026-07-03 at 15:00 with 2 days in transit ships Tuesday 2026-07-07 and is delivered Thursday 2026-07-09. Booked Wednesday 2026-07-01 at 09:00 with 1 day in transit ships that day and is delivered Thursday 2026-07-02.
